observation: S8 predictive effects were below the fixed practical threshold and its economic gate failed; S9 and S10 have no market result. Existing public ETF evidence is narrow and current-vintage, while S10 specialists share finite historical support and weakly differentiated information.
hypothesized_cause: A narrow survivor-ETF sample, weak specialist diversity, sparse context and forecast-policy confounding may limit transferable signal. This is a hypothesis, not an established explanation of prior losses.
change: Create separate FREM-S11 using historical release vintages of six reconstituted Fama/French size-value portfolios, four causal finite-law specialists, delayed capped score stacking, simple incumbents, revision stress and crossed policy attribution. Preserve all predecessor studies and thresholds.
predicted_effect: Broader reconstituted histories and differentiated specialists may improve forecast stability and reveal whether any gain survives data revisions and simple baselines. Positive performance is not guaranteed.
discriminating_experiment: One fixed two-fold development run on the August 2016 release through July 2016, plus common-cutoff August 2008/2016/2024 revision stress. Primary support requires at least five percent relative energy-score improvement over equal mixing and recency with paired intervals above zero in both folds.
